title: The Lord Will Come, and Not Be Slow
description: The Lord Will Come, and Not Be Slow in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Milton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 285 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Kingdom of God on Earth”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Lord will come, and not be slow; His foot-steps can-not err; Be-fore him right-eous-ness shall go, His roy-al har-bin-ger.

lines: The Lord will come, and not be slow;
His footsteps cannot err;
Before him righteousness shall go,
His royal harbinger.
The nations all whom thou hast made
Shall come, and all shall frame
To bow them low before thee, Lord,
And glorify thy name.
Truth from the earth, like to a flower,
Shall bud and blossom then,
And Justice, from her heavenly bower,
Look down on mortal men.
Thee will I praise, O Lord, my God,
Thee honor and adore
With my whole heart, and blaze abroad
Thy name for evermore.
For great thou art, and wonders great
By thy strong hand are done:
Thou, in thy everlasting seat,
Remainest God alone.

licence: Public domain: John Milton died in 1674.
credits: Words by John Milton (1608–1674), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
